episodes.linkedin_post:
Episode 04: 5-minute read. Zero fluff : MCP Goes Stateless: The Biggest Protocol Rewrite Since Launch

MCP ships 7 breaking changes on Jul 28. Sessions removed. Handshake removed. OAuth hardened. HTTP+SSE deprecated. If you only prep for the stateless core, the other 6 will blindside you.

Key findings/points:
- initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id completely removed (SEP-2575, SEP-2567)
- Caching with ttlMs replaces server-sent change notifications
- New Extensions framework replaces Roots, Sampling, and Logging
- One migration report: -412 lines, +168 lines - statelessness mostly means deleting code

The takeaway? If you run remote HTTP MCP servers, start testing against the RC now. stdio servers can wait.

Episode 07: 5-minute read. Zero fluff : VulnHunter: Capital One Built an Agent That Hacks Your Code First

Traditional SAST scanners dump 400 findings. 90% are false positives. Capital One built something that thinks like a pentester instead. Open-sourced it under Apache 2.0.

Key findings/points:
- Built as Claude Code skills (SKILL.md files) - not a standalone tool
- Three-phase pipeline: discover attack surface, write PoC exploit, generate verified fix
- Every finding ships with a working exploit - if it cannot prove exploitability, it does not report it
- Verification loop re-runs the PoC against patched code - no fix ships without proof

The takeaway? SAST scanners search for patterns. VulnHunter reasons like an adversary. One dumps noise. The other proves the bug is real and hands you a tested fix.

episodes.linkedin_post:
Episode 08: 5-minute read. Zero fluff : Ring-Zero: Your Model Has Context Anxiety and Nobody Programmed It

Ant Group trained a 1 trillion parameter model with zero human data. Five cognitive behaviors emerged on their own. One of them is the model panicking about running out of tokens.

Key findings/points:
- Pure RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards) - binary reward, zero human labels
- 5 emergent behaviors: anthropomorphism, structured formatting, self-verification, parallel reasoning, context anxiety
- Context anxiety: at ~85% context usage, the model aborts verification and commits to its best answer
- Naive scaling failed - 3 engineering fixes were required before emergence appeared

The takeaway? Nobody taught this model to panic about tokens. Nobody taught it to verify its own answers. These strategies emerged because they maximize correctness at scale. #1 on HuggingFace Daily Papers.

episodes.linkedin_post:
Episode 11: 5-minute read. Zero fluff : Model Collapse: 1% Synthetic Data Can Poison Your Entire Training Run

Training on AI-generated data causes irreversible distribution collapse. The tails vanish. Rare knowledge disappears. Models progressively converge to producing only the most common outputs. Published in Nature, now confirmed at scale.

Key findings/points:
- 1% synthetic contamination triggers measurable collapse across model families
- Within a few generations of recursive training, models converge to near-identical outputs regardless of prompt
- Tail distributions vanish first: minority languages, rare medical conditions, niche expertise
- 57% of web-scraped parallel text is already machine-translated. The contamination is not hypothetical.

The takeaway? Every training pipeline now needs provenance tracking. If you cannot prove your data is human-generated, assume it is not. The training data moat is real.

episodes.title: IsoDDE: The Drug Discovery AI That Beats Physics Simulations
episodes.linkedin_post:
Episode 12: 5-minute read. Zero fluff : IsoDDE: The Drug Discovery AI That Beats Physics Simulations

Traditional drug discovery takes 10-15 years and $2.6B per approved drug. IsoDDE generates novel drug candidates in hours by learning the energy landscape of protein-ligand binding. It does not dock molecules. It does not screen libraries. It generates them already fitted to the target pocket.

Key findings/points:
- SE(3)-equivariant diffusion: generates molecules that respect 3D rotational and translational symmetry
- Orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics simulations (100-1000x speedup)
- Binding affinity predictions approaching sub-1 kcal/mol of experimental accuracy
- Generates novel scaffolds with drug-like properties, not just variations of known compounds

The takeaway? Physics simulations are accurate but take weeks per candidate. IsoDDE trades brute-force physics for learned energy landscapes. The molecules it generates already fit. That changes the economics of drug discovery.

The EU adopted the AI Act in 2024, started enforcing banned practices in February 2025. Then in July 2026, they published a Digital Omnibus that rewrites definitions, shifts deadlines, and expands exemptions. Mid-enforcement. Companies that spent millions on compliance are now reading a new rulebook.

Key findings/points:
- "AI system" definition narrowed: deterministic rule-based software no longer automatically classified as AI
- Open-source exemption expanded: models released under OSI-approved licenses get lighter obligations
- High-risk compliance deadline pushed to December 2027, giving providers an extra year
- New sandbox provisions: regulatory sandboxes in every member state, SME fast-track access

The takeaway? If you build or deploy AI in Europe, your compliance roadmap just changed. The law you were following got rewritten while you were following it. Read the Omnibus before your next board update.

episodes.title: Photon-1: 18 Years of Screen Recordings Built One World Simulator
episodes.linkedin_post:
Episode 14: 5-minute read. Zero fluff : Photon-1: 18 Years of Screen Recordings Built One World Simulator

Induction Labs trained a 106B sparse MoE on 18 years of raw desktop screen recordings. Zero action labels. The model does not generate video. It simulates environments with physics, object permanence, and cause-effect. Then it transfers to domains it has never seen.

Key findings/points:
- 106B sparse MoE, trained on raw desktop video with zero manual annotation
- Processes frames as latent tokens, not pixels: 30x less compute than comparable dense models
- Emergent world modeling: tracks object permanence, predicts physics, models cause and effect
- Zero-shot transfer: plays checkers and predicts billiard physics despite seeing only desktop recordings during pretraining

The takeaway? Video generators create plausible pixels. World simulators create plausible futures. Photon-1 learned enough about how things work from desktop recordings to simulate billiard collisions better than an LLM trained on 20 trillion text tokens.

Episode 15: 5-minute read. Zero fluff : MiniCPM-Robot: A 0.9B Model That Tracks You on a Robot Dog

OpenBMB shrunk a multimodal VLM to 0.9 billion parameters and deployed it on a quadruped robot dog. Verbal commands. Person tracking through occlusions. Obstacle avoidance. Everything runs on-device with no cloud dependency.

Key findings/points:
- 0.9B parameters, runs on NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX at 5+ FPS with approximately 180ms latency
- Built on MiniCPM4-0.5B base with DINOv3+SigLIP vision encoder
- End-to-end pipeline: speech recognition, visual grounding, person re-identification, locomotion
- Tracks targets through full occlusions: maintains identity when target disappears behind obstacles and re-emerges

The takeaway? Cloud-dependent robots fail when the network drops. On-device robots fail when the model is too big. OpenBMB found the sweet spot: small enough to run locally, capable enough to track, navigate, and follow instructions.
